objective: Analyze a radical function's domain and range and verify an inverse on the correct restricted domain.
assessmentPolicy: Four critical checkpoint items sample domain analysis, transformations, restricted inverses, and reasoning audits. Every item must pass without assistance. The 32 named practice variants expose the full item-family coverage; one checkpoint does not claim to test every variant.

coverage.skill: Distinguish principal even roots, all equation solutions, signed odd roots, and zero.
instruction: A root symbol assigns one value
Read exponents in the real-number setting
examples: Principal value and all equation solutions
A signed fifth-root anchor
coverage.retrieval: Explain the absolute value in an even root of an even power.

coverage.skill: Find transformed root domains and ranges with independent inside and outside reflections.
instruction: Separate the inside restriction from the outside range
examples: Negative inside scale
Negative outside scale
A signed fifth-root anchor
coverage.retrieval: Separate which coefficient controls each interval direction.

coverage.skill: Map anchors, lengths, reflections, and included endpoints for even and odd roots.
examples: Negative inside scale
Negative outside scale
Fourth-root scaling
coverage.retrieval: Reconstruct the transformed anchor map without a memorized direction rule.

coverage.skill: Combine rational sign conditions with original exclusions and numerator versus denominator root rules.
instruction: Use the sign of a rational radicand
A root in a denominator changes the endpoint rule
examples: A rational radicand with two allowed pieces
Move the even root into a denominator
A canceled factor leaves a hole
Odd roots retain division restrictions
A singleton and an empty radical domain
When quotient splitting fails
coverage.retrieval: Find the domain of the reciprocal root in the lesson's recall prompt and explain both exclusions.

coverage.skill: Distinguish inverse relations and functions, and select a valid even-power branch.
instruction: An inverse function needs a one-to-one original
Derive the inverse and select its sign from the branch
examples: Right-branch inverse of a shifted quadratic
The same formula on the left branch
A downward parabola still needs the right sign
A restricted fourth power
coverage.retrieval: Invert the left quadratic in the recall prompt, including both inverse sets and an interior value.

coverage.skill: Retain the inverse domain even when its formula is a polynomial extension.
instruction: A root can invert to a restricted polynomial
examples: A root inverse must keep its restricted input set
coverage.retrieval: Test a target outside the original range and explain why a real polynomial result is insufficient.

coverage.skill: Verify both compositions on their own domains, preserving absolute values and intermediate restrictions.
instruction: Check both composition orders on their own starting domains
Use absolute value to verify a left branch
examples: Prove both identities on the left branch
One composition hides a folded input
An inverse domain that is too small
coverage.retrieval: Prove both recall compositions, check an endpoint, and supply a counterexample to a wrong branch.

coverage.skill: Invert transformed odd powers with signed roots and distinguish exact identities from rounded displays.
instruction: Odd powers reverse without a branch choice
examples: A decreasing cubic and an approximate intermediate
coverage.retrieval: Explain why a transformed odd power is invertible and why that does not hold for every odd-degree polynomial.

coverage.skill: Interpret reflected coordinate pairs and finite graph windows.
instruction: Reflect ordered pairs across the diagonal
examples: Reflect exact coordinate pairs
coverage.independentCheck: mth-restricted-inverse:mixed requires inverse evaluations consistent with exchanged pairs
coverage.retrieval: Exchange one interior point and one endpoint without using a plotted window as a domain.

coverage.skill: Distinguish inverse and reciprocal values, domains, and operations.
instruction: Inverse notation is different from a reciprocal
examples: Recover an input or take a reciprocal
coverage.retrieval: Contrast the multiplication check for a reciprocal with the composition check for an inverse.

coverage.skill: Reject extraneous even-power candidates and explain whether failure is a domain or sign issue.
instruction: Reject candidates that only satisfy a powered equation
examples: An extraneous root that is still in the radical domain
coverage.retrieval: Record both the radical domain and the required sign before squaring.

coverage.skill: Map a finite physical domain to the inverse input window and reject out-of-window extrapolations.
instruction: Carry units and operating limits through an inverse
examples: An inverse with a finite operating window
coverage.retrieval: State both quantity units and both interval restrictions before interpreting an algebraic inverse value.
